newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end narrowly mixed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end narrowly mixed in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended a lackluster session narrowly mixed, as U.S. bonds retreated on light long liquidation after the U.S. Treasury's $10 billion 10-year note auction, traders and analysts said.
"The Street found itself a little long after the auction," one bond futures trader said.

While the 6.50 percent yield was in-line with traders expectations, several bond futures traders said dealers expressed some disappointment with the auction. One trader said the market was expecting an Asian account to buy $1.5 billion of the $10 billion notes available.
"We heard this account was supposed to be switching out of bunds into bonds, but they never showed up," one bond futures floor source said.
One futures trader attributed the December T-bond's advance to the daily high of 111-15/32 on expectations for good demand for the notes.
"The New York community got long," a cash trader said. "Then you saw some nervous Nellies come in and start selling at 6.50 percent. We haven't traded back to that level since."
December T-bonds fell off its highs on light profit-taking. Two firms were scale-down buyers, traders said.

While 6.50 percent was the lowest yield produced from a 10-year auction since February 7, some traders pointed out the softness in the noncompetitive bids. Noncomp bids totaled $284 million, versus $385 million at each of the two previous 10-year note sales.

Talk of weak demand for the auction circulated throughout the Eurodollar futures pit soon after the opening. Some Eurodollar futures traders were looking for the 10-year note yield to climb to 6.55 percent after the auction.
December and March Eurodollars held above support levels of 94.30 and 94.22, respectively.

Rumors of central bank selling and central bank buying, as well as talk of swaps out of mortgages and into U.S. Treasuries, helped keep both bonds and Eurodollars gently swaying within their narrow intraday ranges.
Some traders said comments from Alfred Broaddus, Richmond Federal Reserve president, and Gary Stern, Minneapolis Federal Reserve president, put a slight bid into the market.
Broaddus said he sees some signs of the U.S. economy slowing in retail sales and jobs growth.
"We did make intraday highs on their comments, but volume is so low," one Eurodollar futures trader said.
Estimated volume for Eurodollar futures was estimated at 180,000 contracts, he said.
The market had little reaction to the weekly Redbook retail sales index, which fell 0.4 percent as expected.
U.S. August wholesale inventory numbers will be released at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT on Wednesday.

At the end of pit trade, December T-bonds were down 02/32 at 111-03/32, December 10-year notes were off 02/32 at 108-14/32, March T-bills were flat at 94.80, and December Eurodollars and March Euros were also unchanged at 94.36 and 94.28, respectively.
